subject: Follow-up: model mix & target $/1M tokens — numbers from discovery
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@datafin.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: model mix & target $/1M tokens — numbers from discovery

Alex — thanks again for the call today, great conversation. Per our discussion I wanted to capture the numbers you gave and propose a simple model-split hypothesis and next steps so we can get a scoped estimate to share with procurement.

Recap of your on-call guidance (please correct if I’ve misunderstood):
- Primary use: customer support assistant embedded in DataFin web app (session-based chat).
- Secondary: semantic search/agent embeddings for knowledge base (~monthly reindex + per-query lookups).
- Occasional: reranking for search results when precision matters.
- Budget range: $6k–$12k/month initially for hosted inference (targeting <$1.5k per 1M tokens as a target cost figure to make the unit economics work).
- Expected growth: pilot month -> live month 3 = ~3x active user scale.

Numbers you gave on the call: monthly active sessions ~12k, avg messages per session ~3, avg token length per user message+assistant response ~1,000 tokens (combined). Embedding calls ~25k vectors/month. Rerank calls ~6k/month.

My working model-split (for an initial estimate):
- Chat (90% of token volume): 1.0M tokens per week -> ~4M tokens/month (pilot).
- Embeddings (10% of volume but lower token count): 25k vectors/month (~25k tokens estimated).
- Rerank: small token volume but higher cost per op — estimated 200k tokens/month equivalent.

Target ask: please confirm the numbers above (sessions, tokens per exchange, and the budget range). If that aligns, I’ll attach a quick per-model unit-cost estimate and two pricing options (hosted standard & committed capacity) for you and procurement to review.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm/correct the counts above (sessions/message length/embedding volume).
2) I’ll send a short spreadsheet with 3 scenarios (pilot, steady-state month 3, and 6-month growth) showing token volumes, per-model split, and estimated $/month at two price points (list + 20% committed discount).
3) If the $/1M tokens target is hard ($1k–$1.5k), we can discuss quantization or a dedicated pool (Redwood Dedicated) as option B.

Attachment: I’ve included a draft "redwood-estimate-breakdown.xlsx" (pilot scenario) for quick review.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the confirmations and will prepare the spreadsheet.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez

- Sessions: 12k is for active trial users; expected pilot active = ~4k (we misstated during the call).
- Avg tokens: more like 800 tokens per interaction (combined).
- Embeddings: 25k vectors/month is right, but we also expect a one-time bulk reindex of ~200k vectors at kickoff.

Please update the spreadsheet with these numbers. Also please call out a scenario where we use a cheaper chat model for low-latency quick replies and a higher-quality model for long-form responses (we discussed a model-tiering approach).

Appreciate it — Alex

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding the clarification from Alex. Procurement guardrail $8k/month for pilot, corrected traffic figures below. Please review and help me assemble two quick scenarios in the attached spreadsheet:

Updated inputs (from Alex):
- Pilot active: 4k sessions/month
- Avg tokens/interaction: 800 tokens
- Messages/session: 3 (so ~2,400 tokens/session/month?) — note: tokens are per interaction, not per session, so per-session total = messages * 800 = 2.4k tokens; multiply by sessions for monthly volume.
- Embeddings: 25k vectors/month + 200k initial reindex spike
- Rerank: 10k ops/month
- Leadership target for pilot spend: $8k/month (preferred)

Please build two options: A) Hosted with model-tiering (cheaper chat model for quick replies + higher-quality model for longer responses) and list per-model token-unit-costs; B) Committed 6-month Dedicated pool with 20% off list and potential quantization on the larger chat model.

Karthik — can you propose a plausible tiering split for chat traffic? My suggestion: 70% low-cost chat (short replies), 30% high-quality (long responses & escalations). That should materially change the unit economics.

I’ve attached the draft workbook (redwood-estimate-breakdown.xlsx) with the original numbers; please update and return by EOD so I can send final to Alex and procurement.

— Diego

Diego / Marissa / Alex — quick run at numbers and a suggested split. I updated the attached tab in the workbook. Key assumptions below so procurement has something concrete:

Assumptions (pilot month):
- Pilot sessions: 4,000
- Messages/session: 3 -> total interactions = 12,000
- Avg tokens/interaction: 800 -> total chat tokens = 9.6M tokens/month
- Embeddings: 25k vectors/month (~25k tokens/month) + initial reindex spike of 200k vectors (~200k tokens one-time)
- Rerank: 10k ops/month -> estimated 300k tokens equivalent/month (model-dependent)

Model-tiering proposal (chat):
- Low-cost chat model (short replies): 70% of interactions -> 6.72M tokens/month
- High-quality chat model (long responses, escalate flows): 30% -> 2.88M tokens/month

Unit-cost guidance (hosted list):
- Low-cost chat model: $900 / 1M tokens
- High-quality chat model: $2,400 / 1M tokens
- Embeddings (dense vectors): $1,800 / 1M tokens-equivalent
- Rerank: $2,200 / 1M tokens-equivalent

Estimated pilot spend (hosted list):
- Low-cost chat: 6.72 * $900 = $6,048
- High-quality chat: 2.88 * $2,400 = $6,912
- Embeddings (month): 0.025 * $1,800 = $45
- Rerank: 0.3 * $2,200 = $660
- Total = ~$13,665 / month (hosted list prices)

Committed option (6-month Dedicated, 20% discount + quantization for low-cost model):
- Low-cost chat effective: $720 / 1M -> 6.72 * $720 = $4,838
- High-quality chat (20% off): $1,920 -> 2.88 * $1,920 = $5,530
- Embeddings: $1,440 -> 0.025 * $1,440 = $36
- Rerank: $1,760 -> 0.3 * $1,760 = $528
- Total = ~$10,932 / month (committed, with quantization applied to low-cost model)

Observations:
- Hosted list pricing exceeds Alex’s $8k pilot guardrail by ~70% — so we should lead with the committed option in procurement conversations.
- If Alex’s team can reduce the high-quality chat share to 20% (from 30%), hosted list total drops by ~1.44k/month (~$12.2k total), and the committed option moves closer to the $8k target.

Next steps (concrete):
1) Diego: share the updated workbook with Alex (I updated the scenario tab).
2) Alex: confirm whether 20% high-quality chat is acceptable for pilot or whether certain flows must be high-quality from day 1.
3) Marissa: I can draft a short note for procurement with the committed option terms and a rough timeline for a 6-month Dedicated PO.

If helpful I can also spin up a quick cost comparison slide for procurement that shows break-even points vs. user growth.

— Karthik
